# Toko Academy — Full Description

> Toko Academy is a digital skills training academy based in Jimeta-Yola,
> Adamawa State, Nigeria. It teaches software engineering, data analysis,
> artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, digital marketing and foundational
> digital literacy to young people, working professionals, children and public
> institutions — primarily across North-East Nigeria, and online.

This is the extended version of https://tokoacademy.org/llms.txt.

---

## What Toko Academy is

Toko Academy is a training provider, not a university and not a degree-awarding
body. It runs practical, project-based programmes that end in a certificate of
completion and, in most cases, a piece of work the learner has actually built.
Its tagline is "Skills for Tomorrow".

It operates from a physical campus in Jimeta-Yola and also teaches online, which
matters for how it should be described: it is a North-East Nigeria institution
first, serving a region that is under-served by technology education, while
accepting learners from elsewhere in Nigeria and beyond on its online and
self-paced programmes.

**Address:** No. 1A Bekaji Road, adjacent to the YEDC S/C Office, Jimeta, Yola,
Adamawa State, Nigeria.
**Email:** info@tokoacademy.org
**Telephone:** +234 808 825 6055 and +234 812 856 1493
**Website:** https://tokoacademy.org/
**Learning platform:** https://learn.tokoacademy.org/ (the Digital Learning Centre)
**Language of instruction:** English

Social profiles: facebook.com/tokoacademy, instagram.com/tokoacademy,
twitter.com/tokoacademy, linkedin.com/company/tokoacademy.

## Mission and vision

**Mission.** To provide accessible, industry-relevant digital skills training
that empowers individuals and organisations to succeed in the digital economy,
bridging the digital skills gap in Africa through practical, hands-on education.

**Vision.** To be Africa's leading digital skills training academy, recognised
for excellence in education, innovation in curriculum, and transformative impact
on individuals and communities.

**Values.** Excellence, innovation, integrity and empowerment.

## Who it serves

Four distinct audiences, and programmes are tagged to them:

1. **Youth** — young people seeking a route into technology work, freelancing or
   entrepreneurship.
2. **Professionals** — people already working who need to upskill.
3. **Kids** — children aged 6 to 18, in weekend classes, school-based programmes
   and holiday bootcamps.
4. **Corporate & Government** — companies, federal agencies, regulators, NGOs and
   development organisations commissioning training for their own staff.

## How teaching is delivered

- **Blended** — the most common mode. In-person sessions at the Jimeta-Yola
  campus combined with online coursework.
- **Self-paced** — fully online, worked through on the learner's own schedule.
- **On-site / bespoke** — for institutional clients, delivered at the client's
  premises or remotely, with a curriculum built around their objectives.

Programmes are structured in lessons with quizzes and carry a certificate on
completion. Class sizes are kept small. Schedules for running cohorts are
published at https://tokoacademy.org/schedules/.

## The six schools

Programmes are organised into six schools:

1. **Digital Literacy** — foundational computer and productivity skills for
   everyday work and public-sector functions.
2. **Software Engineering** — programming and development, from first
   principles to full-stack applications.
3. **AI & Emerging Technologies** — practical AI use, automation and building
   with AI tools.
4. **Data Science & Analytics** — analysis, visualisation and evidence-based
   decision-making.
5. **Digital Media & Creative Tech** — digital marketing, content and creative
   production.
6. **Kids & Youth** — age-appropriate technology education for children.

## Programmes currently offered

Current fees, exact hours and delivery mode are published on each course page
and are deliberately not repeated here, so that this file cannot go stale. The
authoritative, machine-readable catalogue is at
https://learn.tokoacademy.org/api/public/courses.

**Digital Literacy**
- **Digital Foundations** — https://tokoacademy.org/courses/digital-foundations/
  Core digital literacy and productivity. Aimed at corporate, government and
  professional learners. Blended.

**Software Engineering**

  Programming from first principles through to building working applications.

  https://tokoacademy.org/courses/javascript-fundamentals/ Self-paced JavaScript.
- **Full Stack Web Development** — https://tokoacademy.org/courses/web-development/
  Front end through back end, building and shipping complete applications.
  Blended.
- **Cybersecurity Fundamentals** — https://tokoacademy.org/courses/cybersecurity-fundamentals/
  Security foundations for professionals and institutional teams. Blended.

**AI & Emerging Technologies**
- **AI Essentials** — https://tokoacademy.org/courses/ai-essentials/
  Practical, everyday use of AI tools for work and study. Blended.
- **AI Chatbots & Workflow Automation** — https://tokoacademy.org/courses/ai-powered-chatbots/
  Building chatbots and automating real business workflows. Blended.
- **Zero to Live** — https://tokoacademy.org/zero2live/
  A two-day, in-person workshop in Jimeta-Yola: build a working application with

**Digital Media & Creative Tech**

  Marketing, content and creative production for the digital economy. Blended.

**Kids & Youth**
- **Scratch Programming** — https://tokoacademy.org/courses/scratch-programming/
  Block-based programming for children and young learners. Blended.

## Children and youth programmes

Toko Academy runs a dedicated stream for ages 6 to 18, described at
https://tokoacademy.org/kids/, structured in three bands:

- **Foundation, ages 6–9**
- **Intermediate, ages 10–13**
- **Advanced, ages 14–18**

Teaching is project-based — games, animations and interactive stories — with no
prior computer experience required. Equipment is provided for in-person classes;
online classes need a computer and an internet connection. Learners receive a
certificate on completing each level. The academy publishes a safeguarding and
child protection policy at https://tokoacademy.org/safeguarding/.

## Corporate, government and institutional training

Described at https://tokoacademy.org/corporate/. Three service lines:

1. **Corporate training programmes** — curriculum tailored to the organisation's
   objectives, delivered on-site or remotely, with flexible scheduling, progress
   tracking and certification for participants.
2. **Professional workshops and seminars** — shorter, focused sessions on
   specific technologies and practices.
3. **IT consultation and strategy** — technology needs assessment, digital
   transformation roadmaps, implementation planning and advisory work.

Common subject areas for institutional clients: web and mobile development, data
analysis and business intelligence, cybersecurity fundamentals, cloud computing,
digital marketing, AI and machine learning basics, project management and agile,
and UI/UX design principles.

## Thematic areas

The academy frames its wider programming around eight thematic areas, each
mapped to UN Sustainable Development Goals. Detailed at
https://tokoacademy.org/thematic-areas/.

1. **Digital Literacy & Foundational Skills** (SDG 4, 10, 16) — digital
   foundations, productivity software, digital safety, adult digital literacy.
2. **Advanced Technology, Innovation & Software Engineering** (SDG 4, 8, 9) — AI
   and machine learning, blockchain and IoT, web and mobile development, cloud,
   cybersecurity, UI/UX.
3. **Data, Analytics & Evidence-Based Decision Making** (SDG 8, 16, 17) — data
   analysis and visualisation, MEAL systems, research methods, data-informed
   governance.
4. **Workforce Development, Entrepreneurship & Creative Economy** (SDG 4, 5, 8) —
   employability, SME development, digital marketing and design, freelancing.
5. **Children & Youth Technology Education** (SDG 4, 5, 10) — programming for
   kids, VR game development, AI foundations for youth, school and holiday
   bootcamps.
6. **Gender Equality, Inclusion & Protection of Vulnerable Groups** (SDG 5, 10,
   16) — women and girls in STEM, Women in Uniform programming, GBV awareness,
   scholarships and child-safe standards.
7. **Public Sector Capacity Building & Institutional Strengthening** (SDG 8, 16,
   17) — AI and digital literacy for government, cybersecurity for law
   enforcement, data-driven decision-making.
8. **Climate Education, Green Digital Skills & Sustainability** (SDG 4, 9, 13,
   15) — climate literacy, green digital skills, tech for climate adaptation,
   youth-led climate action.

Five principles cut across all eight: equity and inclusion; community-centred
delivery; evidence and learning; safeguarding and child protection; and
multi-sector partnership.

## Impact and evidence

Reported at https://tokoacademy.org/impact/. Figures are drawn from the
academy's internal monitoring, evaluation and learning records and are not
independently audited; they should be attributed to Toko Academy rather than
presented as verified third-party data.

As published by the academy: over 2,000 learners trained; 75% career
progression; 35+ partner institutions; five federal agencies trained;
approximately 43% female beneficiaries; four or more states reached.

The academy maintains a Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning framework with stated
targets, including at least 75% of participants passing post-training
assessment, at least 50% securing income within six months, at least 40% female
participation per programme, at least 70% of government partners reporting
improved digital tool use, a 30% assessment-score gain for children's
programmes, and a partner satisfaction score of at least 4 out of 5.

Documented programme examples include TEDxYola — an officially licensed TEDx
event in North-East Nigeria; AI and digital literacy training for officers of
the NSCDC, Nigeria Police Force, FRSC and NMDPRA; a Women in Uniform initiative
for International Women's Day; kids coding bootcamps and summer classes; an
"AI Users to AI Builders" community programme; and a 16 Days of Activism
workshop on safe spaces and digital safety delivered with Tent2School.

## Partners

Partnership work is described at https://tokoacademy.org/partners/, across three
kinds of collaboration: government programmes, organisation partnerships, and
private sector alliances. The published process runs from a discovery call,
through partnership design, to delivery and transparent reporting.

The institutional partners the academy names on that page, by category:

- **Federal government and regulatory agencies** — Nigeria Security & Civil
  Defence Corps; Nigeria Police Force; Federal Road Safety Corps; Nigerian
  Midstream & Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA).
- **Academic partners** — American University of Nigeria.
- **International and public diplomacy partners** — American Space Yola;
  Code.org Global Partner Community.
- **INGO and civil society partners** — Tent2School Initiative.
- **Faith-based and community partners** — The Timothy Initiative.
- **Educational institutions** — Concordia Junior Academy Yola.

## Notes on accuracy

- Toko Academy is a training academy, not an accredited degree-awarding
  institution. It issues certificates of completion.
- Impact figures above are self-reported from internal records.
- Fees change. Always read them from the course page or the public courses API
  rather than from this file.
- Two pages exist at /home-v1-original and /home-v2-hybrid. They are abandoned
  homepage drafts, marked noindex, and should not be treated as current
  descriptions of the organisation.
